story_title: As an Event Coordinator, I want the system to check whether a venue is suitable for my event so that I can avoid selecting venues that cannot meet its requirements

acceptance_criteria.text: The system compares expected attendance against the venue's capacity for the event's selected room layout, not a single venue-wide figure.
The system checks required facilities against available venue facilities.
The system checks required accessibility features.
The system checks required room layout.
A venue that fails a mandatory requirement is identified as unsuitable.
The system clearly indicates which requirement is not met.

open_questions: The suitability check is not built on branch SPM-41-check-venue-suitability yet. These cases follow the 'Find a venue' mockup (design/mockups/VenueSearch.dc.html): a Find a venue page opened from the event, a Suitable / Too small / Partial match badge, and reason lines such as 'Capacity 300 — your event expects 450.' and 'Missing: hearing loop.' Confirm the entry point, badge labels and reason wording; the expected results are worded loosely until then.
The mockup labels a failing venue 'Too small' or 'Partial match', while AC5 says 'unsuitable'. Should there be one explicit 'Unsuitable' label?
The mockup shows a 'Request anyway' button on venues that fail. AC5 only says such a venue is identified as unsuitable. Should a coordinator still be able to request one?
The mockup's Marina Grand Hall shows theatre capacity 300, but seed data has Theatre 500 (max 500). Cases use the seed data.
Seed data has Jurong Training Room with a Theatre layout of 70 but a max capacity of 60. Is a layout allowed to exceed the venue's max capacity? Cases avoid that layout.

The schema (EventFacilityRequirement.isMandatory) says a nice-to-have facility must NOT disqualify a venue, but the event form and API only ever create mandatory requirements, so a tester cannot set one from the UI. No case written. Is there a way to mark a requirement optional, and should AC5's 'mandatory' wording be tested through it?

AC3 says the system checks required accessibility features. The event's free-text 'Accessibility notes' cannot be matched against a venue; only ticked accessibility facilities can. Is checking the ticked features what AC3 intends?
What should the check do for a draft event with no expected attendance or no preferred layout: show 'incomplete', treat as passing, or block the check? No case written.
For multi-session events, each session has its own attendance and layout. Should the check run per session and name the failing session? No case written.
A venue with no layouts is described in src/app/venues/page.tsx as 'never offered by venue search'. Should it instead be shown as unsuitable with a reason (layout not offered)?
Venue availability (existing bookings) and opening hours are not mentioned in these acceptance criteria. All cases assume a date with no bookings. Confirm they are out of scope for SPM-41.

RESOLVED: the same 'SPM41 …' event name was originally reused across test cases with conflicting attendance/layout/facility values (e.g. 'SPM41 Training Day' needed 60, 55, 70 and 71 attendees at once). Each test case now targets its own uniquely-named event, seeded in prisma/seed.ts (organiser Rachel Ng, coordinator Priya Raj, status Under review, ~15 Mar 2027), so no manual event creation is needed before running these cases.
